title: OKR Hub Orchestration and Cross-Team Gating Protocol
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose:
Create an operational 'OKR Hub' and formal gating protocol that makes company-level objectives actionable across Engineering, Product, Design and GTM teams. The Hub is a lightweight synthesis layer that: 1) codifies initiative ownership and dependency surfaces, 2) enforces gating rules for rollouts and external commitments, and 3) provides a single view for escalation and tradeoff decisions when cross-team capacity conflicts arise.

Background / problem statement:
We repeatedly observe the same failure modes during quarterly execution: duplicate work across teams, missed implicit dependencies (e.g., telemetry and SLO hooks), and late discovery of resource conflicts that force scope cuts. Existing OKR docs are centralized but not operational — teams treat them as signals rather than a gating contract. We need an instrumented mechanism to translate company objectives into timeboxed, dependency-aware commitments with clear reversal and escalation rules.

Goals (SMART):
- Reduce cross-team unplanned rework by 40% for company-level initiatives in Q2 2025.
- Surface >=95% of critical technical dependencies two weeks before sprint start for initiatives tied to company OKRs.
- Standardize a gating workflow used by at least 5 cross-functional initiatives in Q2 pilot.

Success metrics (how we'll measure):
- Count of dependency-related rollbacks or scope trims per initiative (target: -40% vs Q1 baseline).
- Time between dependency discovery and mitigation action (target: median <= 14 days).
- Adoption: number of initiatives adopting OKR Hub templates and gating checklist (target: >=5).

Scope (in):
- Define OKR Hub artifact templates (initiative card, dependency graph, gating checklist, rollback policy).
- Integrate the Hub with Linear ticket fields and Redwood Console dashboards (links + SLO tags).
- Onboard 5 pilot initiatives across Eng/Product/Design.
- Publish the cross-team gating runbook and training session.

Scope (out):
- Company-wide automation of enforcement (future work).
- Changes to compensation or formal promotion criteria.

Approach / deliverables:
1) Design: a 1-page Initiative Card template (owner, outcomes, success metrics, dependencies, minimum bar to launch).
2) Tooling: small Linear template plus a Confluence hub page and lightweight dashboard in Console showing initiative status and unresolved dependencies.
3) Process: a gating checklist and 3-level escalation ladder (owner -> cross-team lead -> exec sponsor).
4) Pilot: run with 5 initiatives during Cycle 10; collect feedback and iterate.

Decision trade-offs discussed:
- Strict enforcement vs. pragmatic adoption: we will prefer a pragmatic, education-first approach for the pilot; hard enforcement will be re-evaluated after adoption metrics are met.
- Centralized vs. federated dependency tracking: start centralized in the Hub for clarity; shift to federated automated signals in a later phase.

Deliverable links and artifacts:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/OKR+Hub+Draft
- Linear templates: https://linear.app/redwood/board/templates/okr-hub-template
- Console dashboard mock: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1OKRHubMock
- Sample initiative card (pilot): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1PilotCard

Acceptance criteria (minimum):
- Initiative Card template published in Confluence and linked from Linear templates.
- Linear template created and used by 5 pilot initiatives.
- Dashboard shows at least one dependency per pilot initiative and a live gating status.
- Gating runbook reviewed and approved by Eng Director and Head of Product.
